data.title: Validate an export before engine handoff
data.summary: One GLB, its source identity and the existing project's Khronos validator. An LLM-assisted recipe with a concrete practice case, visual procedure and review gates.

facts.text: Khronos glTF Validator produces issue reports against the glTF specification.

prerequisites: An authorized Claude Code / Codex / existing Studio environment and a recorded tool version. Blender-specific references here are pinned to the 4.5 manual; check differences in your installed version.
Practice inputs: One GLB, its source identity and the existing project's Khronos validator.

Permission to use the source assets and a writable derived-output location. Use a disposable project copy for edits. An MCP connection is optional; reviewed scripts or manual tool actions can follow the same procedure.
steps: Inspect the existing project, asset registry and target runtime for an equivalent export validator workflow. Reuse the closest source and preserve its original files.

Give Claude Code, Codex or another authorized coding assistant this practice brief: One GLB, its source identity and the existing project's Khronos validator. Ask for a small plan and parameter/script diff; verify names and APIs against the installed tool version before applying it.
Export a derived candidate without overwriting the authoring source
Run the existing validator and retain errors, warnings and extension requirements
Import in the actual destination and inspect scale, materials, animation and required decoders

Save the derived candidate separately, record software versions and source/output identities, then perform the acceptance checks. Keep unresolved quality, performance and rights questions in the receipt.
data.output: A versioned validate an export before engine handoff candidate, the input/parameter table, source identity and a review receipt with the checks below.
validation: Validation errors are resolved or explicitly block delivery
A zero-error report is accompanied by a destination import check
Record actual observations separately from expected results; missing tests remain unrun.
limitations: A valid file is not proof of visual acceptance or broad engine compatibility.
Sintra-authored proposal, not an executed Blender/engine/solver test. The diagram illustrates the procedure and is not a render or execution receipt.
Cloud chat cannot directly control a local 3D app without an appropriate authorized bridge. Tool access, model availability, paid services and rendering resources must be checked separately.
tips: Keep validator version and source hash beside its report.
Let the LLM draft and explain bounded changes; use deterministic software to measure geometry, calculate trajectories and validate files.

data.prompt: Help me validate an export before engine handoff in [existing authorized project]. First find an equivalent asset/workflow and inspect the installed tool version. Practice brief: One GLB, its source identity and the existing project's Khronos validator. Propose the smallest parameter or script diff and explain each tool action. Follow the linked procedure, preserve original assets and stop on missing inputs or unsupported APIs. Check: Validation errors are resolved or explicitly block delivery; A zero-error report is accompanied by a destination import check. Return actual observations, source/output identities and blockers. Do not call expected results completed tests or publish private source paths.
